questions.question: If "Inhalation Hazard" appears on a shipping paper, what placard should the shipper provide?

options.text: Poison Gas or Poison Inhalation Hazard

questions.correctAnswerText: Poison Gas or Poison Inhalation Hazard
questions.explanation: If "Inhalation Hazard" appears on a shipping paper or package, you must display the "Poison Inhalation Hazard" or "Poison Gas" placard.

questions.question: When transporting Division 1.3 materials, the floor liner should be:
questions.explanation: Use a floor liner when transporting Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 materials. The floor must be tight. The liner must be made from non-metallic material or non-ferrous metal (metals that do not contain iron).

questions.question: Shippers package hazardous materials in order to ____ them.
questions.explanation: Shippers package hazardous materials to contain them completely. Vehicles must display placards to communicate the risk of the cargo.

questions.question: Many products classed as poison are also:
questions.explanation: Many hazardous materials classified as poison are also flammable.

questions.question: Unless a package is clearly unsafe, a driver needs ____ to accept it.
questions.explanation: When a shipper packages hazardous materials, they certify the package meets Hazardous Materials Regulations (HMR). Unless a package is clearly unsafe or does not meet HMR, you can accept the shipper's certification that the package is properly prepared.

questions.question: In addition to reading the manual, the best way to learn about transporting hazardous materials is to:
questions.explanation: The manual has all information needed to pass the hazardous materials test, but it is only the first step. You should also read federal and state rules about transporting hazardous materials and attend training courses.

questions.question: If a shipping paper lists both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, the hazardous materials may need to be:

options.text: Circled by a pen or marker.

questions.explanation: If a shipping paper lists both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, the hazardous ones must be marked in one of three ways: entered first, highlighted in a contrasting color, or marked with an "X" in an "HM" column.

questions.question: What does a driver need to transport hazardous materials?

options.text: A CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement
A CDL with a tank endorsement
A CDL with a cargo endorsement

questions.correctAnswerText: A CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement
questions.explanation: You must have a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement to drive any vehicle used to transport hazardous materials.

questions.question: When transporting hazardous materials, a shipper should warn others by:

options.text: Posting HazMat placards on their truck.
Putting flashing lights on their truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Posting HazMat placards on their truck.
questions.explanation: Shippers of hazardous materials must display diamond-shaped warning signs called placards on the transporting vehicle. Shippers must provide applicable placards, labels, shipping papers, and emergency response information.

questions.question: If a hazardous materials package is too small for a label, it should be labeled:

options.text: By being placed in a certain part of the trailer.

questions.explanation: If a hazardous materials label will not fit on a package, attach it to a tag that is securely fastened to the package.

questions.question: If your engine runs a pump for compressed gas delivery, when should you turn off the engine?
questions.explanation: If your engine runs a pump for product transfer, turn it off after the transfer is complete but before you unhook the hoses.

questions.question: Which of these is a sign that a shipment may contain hazardous materials?

options.text: The shipper deals in fireworks or munitions.
The last shipment you picked up was labeled as hazardous.

questions.correctAnswerText: The shipper deals in fireworks or munitions.
questions.explanation: A sign that a shipment may contain hazardous materials is when the shipper works with these materials. This includes paint dealers, chemical suppliers, pest control businesses, agricultural suppliers, and explosives or fireworks dealers.

questions.question: What shape are hazardous material placards?
questions.explanation: Vehicles carrying hazardous materials must display diamond-shaped warning signs on all four sides. These signs are called placards.

questions.question: Who is responsible for properly labeling hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: The shipper is responsible for packaging, marking, and labeling hazardous materials properly. The driver should verify that the materials are correctly labeled.

questions.question: What can you do with an improperly placarded vehicle?

options.text: It may only be moved in an emergency.
It may be driven if the cargo is not radioactive.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may only be moved in an emergency.
questions.explanation: A vehicle without proper placards for hazardous materials may only be driven if needed to protect life and property in an emergency.

questions.question: How must a hazardous waste manifest be signed?

options.text: On the outside of the trailer

questions.explanation: When transporting hazardous waste, you must carry a Uniform Hazardous Waste Manifest that is signed by hand.

questions.question: What license does a driver need to transport hazardous materials?

options.text: A CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement
A CDL with a tank endorsement

questions.correctAnswerText: A CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement
questions.explanation: To drive any vehicle carrying hazardous materials, you must have a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement.

questions.question: Where should a hazardous material's identification number appear?

options.text: On a sticker near the shipping container

questions.explanation: A material's ID number must appear on its packaging and shipping papers. It must also appear on cargo tanks and other bulk packaging.

questions.question: What does a material's hazard class show?

options.text: The risks associated with the material
How quickly the material must reach its destination

questions.correctAnswerText: The risks associated with the material
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials are placed into one of nine classes. Each class describes the type of risks the material poses.

questions.question: What should a driver check?

options.text: The shipping paper matches the markings and labels on packages
The shipping paper is written in code
All packages are labeled as poison

questions.correctAnswerText: The shipping paper matches the markings and labels on packages
questions.explanation: Compare package markings and labels to the shipping papers. Make sure the shipper has used the correct description on the shipping paper and provided proper labels on the packages.

questions.question: Who must label hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: The shipper is responsible for packaging, marking, and labeling hazardous materials. The shipper must provide warning placards.

questions.question: Shipping papers should be:

options.text: Easily seen by anyone entering the cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: Easily seen by anyone entering the cab.
questions.explanation: Keep shipping papers in a pouch on the driver's side door or in another easy-to-reach location. Anyone entering the cab must be able to see them easily.

questions.question: If a package of explosives has an oily stain or shows dampness, the driver should:

options.text: Use towels to absorb the liquid.

questions.explanation: Never transport damaged packages of explosives. Do not accept any package that is damp or has an oily stain.

questions.question: When applying for an original or renewed HazMat endorsement, you must undergo a background check through which agency?
questions.explanation: For an original or renewed HazMat endorsement, you must complete a federal security threat assessment conducted by the Transportation Security Administration (TSA).

questions.question: Class 1, Class 2.1, and Class 3 materials should not be placed in a trailer with:
questions.explanation: Do not use cargo heaters when transporting Class 1 (Explosives), Class 2.1 (Flammable Gases), or Class 3 (Flammable Liquids) materials in the same space.

questions.question: A shipping paper:

options.text: Is not needed for most shipments of hazardous materials.
Is required for all shipments of hazardous materials.
Can be kept in a digital file.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is required for all shipments of hazardous materials.
questions.explanation: Shippers must provide proper shipping papers for all hazardous materials shipments to communicate the risks.

questions.question: When traveling with Division 1.1 explosives, you may park no closer than ____ from the nearest building.
questions.explanation: Do not park within 300 feet of a bridge, tunnel, or building when carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, unless you need to park temporarily for operational needs like refueling.

questions.question: If a shipping paper describes both hazardous and non-hazardous materials:

options.text: The hazardous materials must be listed first.
The hazardous materials must be written larger.
The hazardous materials must be listed in red ink.

questions.correctAnswerText: The hazardous materials must be listed first.
questions.explanation: When a shipping paper lists both hazardous and non-hazardous materials, always list the hazardous materials first.

questions.question: Load hazardous materials:
questions.explanation: Always load hazardous materials away from heat sources. Follow all regulations about keeping explosives and flammable materials out of cargo spaces with heaters.

questions.question: In general, before loading or unloading any flammable liquids, an engine should be:
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine before loading or unloading flammable liquids, unless the engine is needed to operate a pump. Ground the tank before opening the filling hole and keep it grounded until the hole is closed.
